BL-205.finding: The ordinary path is fixed and tested, but the row's resolution rests on 'an unclaimed slot cannot have opened one', and that is false on the machine surface. One machine key call to the OTP send or answer twin on an unclaimed slot stamps first_opened_at, even when the call then fails with no destination. After that the gate cannot be amended and the claim cannot pass, so the row's original deadlock is back with void() or the wrong-phone claim as the way out; a step deadline may also release the slot. It takes an integrator driving the machine ceremony on a slot it has not claimed, so it is narrow, and only a machine key can do it. The fix is a slot refusal on both twins before recordRecipientOpening (also closes the code-to-unnamed-party door), or exempting unclaimed slots from the alreadyEntered guard. Found by static reading, not executed; a single HTTP test would confirm it. Everything else in the row can be closed.

BL-204.finding: ADR-0096 does answer decision 8's sub-decision as written for clear text and removes the refusal mechanism. It does not answer this row's own case: an identity ABSENT from a fact that decision 7, still standing, says should carry it. A claim is not one of the five members, so the clean slate does not cover it, and §2.6 distinguishes clear from encrypted, not absent. So the row's question stays unanswered: either retire decision 7 for RecipientClaimed and accept ROW_CURRENT identity as final, or require identity on the fact before the first real-data deployment, after which it is unrepairable. ADR-0096's claim of an answer is what a closer would cite, and it reads broader than its sections. Medium confidence because a maintainer may read the row's ask as limited to decision 8; the event's contents are not decided by any accepted section.
